events.detail: orx discover openalex / biorxiv returned exit 1 with 'OpenAlex is rate-limiting requests (429 Too Many Requests); retry in 7178s'. biorxiv routes through OpenAlex and failed identically. Affected plan ids k01, k07, k11 (openalex) and k12, k13 (biorxiv). Europe PMC used as the logged fallback (plan ids e01-e10).

Retried at the end of the run: 'orx discover openalex --no-telemetry "flying fish gliding flight"' -> exit 1, '429 Too Many Requests; retry in 6962s'. OpenAlex was never reached in this run. Nothing was substituted for it from memory.

The first 46 queries were written as 6-12 term natural-language questions and all returned 0 hits except g24,g25,g28,g30,g31. Cause: orx discover pubmed passes the string to NCBI E-utilities, which ANDs every term. The batch is kept in this log because it is a real logged result, not hidden; it was superseded by the short-query batch h01-h50. No citation in this index comes from a g-series call.

Plan ids h40 and m10 were flagged rate-limited by a loose substring test; inspection of raw/pubmed-h40.json shows the match was the page number 'p429' inside an abstract. Both calls succeeded (exit 0, 15 and 9 hits). Corrected here rather than silently.

The first cross-check of 'is this hit already cited by the draft?' compared each hit's PMID against the draft text. orx's PubMed output carries no DOI field, and several threads (physics above all) cite only by DOI, so that check wrongly reported cited works as uncited: e.g. PMID 20833919 (Park & Choi, 'Aerodynamic characteristics of flying fish in gliding flight') is cited by every physics draft as doi:10.1242/jeb.046052. All 550 distinct PubMed PMIDs returned in this run were therefore resolved to DOIs through Europe PMC (batched GETs, all HTTP 200) and the cross-check was re-run on PMID OR DOI. The corrected numbers are the ones reported.

NCBI_EMAIL was unset in the environment passed to every orx call (env.pop). No orx call carried an email, name, ORCID or account id. Every Europe PMC request was a plain curl GET with no email= or tool= parameter. No request in this run contains a personal identifier.
run_identifier is null for every call. 'orx discover' prints a JSON array of hits and issues no run or experiment identifier (same finding as research/prior-art/SEARCHES.md). None was invented.

No query in this run targets bird data. Aves is this project's frozen holdout. The nine holdout drafts are indexed but deliberately NOT literature-grounded, and lean/.../law-thompson1917-ch02-07.trig (ostrich and moa) was left ungrounded for the same reason. Bird titles that appeared incidentally in flying-fish result sets (e.g. PMID 15875570, 35154643) were not opened as data and are not cited.
